signature: The boomers hit their care years — demand floods into everything age-related, but reimbursement cuts and a caregiver shortage cap the upside.

subthemes.title: Joint repair & surgery
subthemes.angle: Aging joints and eyes drive implant and outpatient-surgery volume; robotics is now standard of care but Medicare cuts squeeze the price.

subthemes.title: When the senses fade
subthemes.angle: Hearing and vision decline create steady demand; OTC hearing aids and retail optical reshape who captures it.

subthemes.title: The chronic-disease machine
subthemes.angle: Kidney and heart disease scale with age into recurring, consolidated, reimbursement-dependent care.

subthemes.title: Senior housing at scale
subthemes.angle: Boomer demand meets a bed shortage and a wage spiral; PE rolls up the fragment.

subthemes.title: Care comes home
subthemes.angle: The money rewards keeping seniors out of facilities; home care booms but can't hire fast enough.

subthemes.title: The specialists of old age
subthemes.angle: Age-skewed outpatient specialties ride the demographic wave while fighting reimbursement pressure.

groups.label: C · The money side of aging

subthemes.title: Insuring a longer life
subthemes.angle: Living longer turns into an annuity and long-term-care market — the balance-sheet side of aging.

subthemes.title: The drug that rewrote aging
subthemes.angle: GLP-1 drugs are the biggest force in aging health — remaking weight loss, cardio-metabolic care, and pharma.

subthemes.title: Grey leisure & the active old
subthemes.angle: Wealthy, active retirees spend on experiences and the outdoors — a real growth pocket.

subthemes.title: Who pays for all this
subthemes.angle: Medicare Advantage and insurers hold the purse; benefit cuts and cost control cap every provider's pricing.

subthemes.title: The caregiver shortage
subthemes.angle: The binding constraint isn't demand — it's the aides and nurses to serve it, and wages spiral.

subthemes.title: The graying market
subthemes.angle: Capstone: aging is a guaranteed demand wave, but labor and reimbursement decide who actually profits.

signature: Workers got scarce — wages spiral, the trades can't fill the gap, and whoever can automate or pay up wins while everyone else eats the margin hit.

subthemes.title: The skilled-trades gap
subthemes.angle: An aging trades workforce and few new entrants push wages up faster than contractors can pass them on.

subthemes.title: The people who build things
subthemes.angle: Construction demand meets a structural worker shortage; robots and prefab are the reluctant answer.

subthemes.title: Hands for the infrastructure boom
subthemes.angle: Federal money and mandates create work, but the workers to do it are the bottleneck.

subthemes.title: The care-worker crunch
subthemes.angle: Nurses and aides are the scarce input in a demographically guaranteed-demand sector.

subthemes.title: Clinical labor everywhere
subthemes.angle: Clinician shortages ripple through every corner of outpatient care.

subthemes.title: The driver shortage
subthemes.angle: Trucking's chronic driver churn collides with freight cycles; automation looms but isn't here yet.

subthemes.title: Aviation's people problem
subthemes.angle: Pilots, ground crew, and caterers are scarce and unionized; labor sets the cost floor.

subthemes.title: The hospitality wage spiral
subthemes.angle: Low-wage service work reprices upward; operators automate the counter or eat the margin.

subthemes.title: Automate or eat the margin
subthemes.angle: Where labor can be mechanized, it is; where it can't, margins compress.

subthemes.title: Passing the wages on
subthemes.angle: Service businesses try to pass wage inflation to customers — until price resistance bites.

subthemes.title: The labor squeeze
subthemes.angle: Capstone: labor is the new scarce resource; automation, wages, and consolidation are the three ways out.

signature: Permanent jobs unbundle into gigs, fractional roles, and expert networks — the firm rents talent by the hour, and the platform in the middle takes the cut.

subthemes.title: The expert, on demand
subthemes.angle: Companies rent senior judgment by the call or the project instead of hiring it full-time.

subthemes.title: Fractional leadership
subthemes.angle: Fractional CFOs, CMOs, and coaches replace full-time executives at smaller firms.

subthemes.title: Advice as a rented service
subthemes.angle: Whole functions — HR, marketing, compliance — get rented from consultants instead of staffed.

groups.label: B · The platforms in the middle

subthemes.title: Who places the talent
subthemes.angle: Recruiters and brokers monetize the matching as work fragments.

subthemes.title: Selling the credential
subthemes.angle: Short-course and certification providers sell the fast credentials the gig market rewards.

subthemes.title: The benefits gap
subthemes.angle: Fractional work shifts benefits and stability onto the worker; insurers reprice the risk.

subthemes.title: The firm gets thinner
subthemes.angle: Professional firms lean on contractors and offshoring, thinning the permanent core.

subthemes.title: The fractional worker
subthemes.angle: Capstone: the unit of work shrinks from the job to the task; platforms and specialists win, stability loses.

signature: GLP-1 drugs, the sober-curious wave, and the retreat from sugar are rewriting what people eat and drink — volume shrinks, and only the health-aligned or premium survive.

groups.label: A · The drug that changed appetite

subthemes.title: The GLP-1 shockwave
subthemes.angle: Weight-loss drugs cut appetite and are already reshaping food, drink, and weight-loss demand.

subthemes.title: Snacking under siege
subthemes.angle: Indulgent, calorie-dense categories face structural demand pressure as appetites shrink and scrutiny rises.

subthemes.title: The sober-curious wave
subthemes.angle: Younger drinkers drink less; alcohol venues and makers face a structural, not cyclical, decline.

subthemes.title: Spirits in contraction
subthemes.angle: A boom-to-bust hangover: gluts, tariffs, and moderation hit premium spirits hard.

subthemes.title: Functional & better-for-you drinks
subthemes.angle: Sugar-free, functional, and 'better-for-you' positioning is the only growth lane left in beverages.

subthemes.title: When diet meets convenience
subthemes.angle: Health-conscious, convenient eating reshuffles who wins in packaged and prepared food.

subthemes.title: What you drink now
subthemes.angle: Coffee, milk alternatives, and snacks reposition around health and premium to hold volume.

subthemes.title: Fast food's reckoning
subthemes.angle: Value and indulgence collide with health scrutiny and GLP-1; chains reformulate or lose share.

subthemes.title: Regulation & the warning label
subthemes.angle: Health warnings, sugar rules, and scrutiny become a cost and a repositioning trigger.

subthemes.title: The health reckoning
subthemes.angle: Capstone: wellness and weight-loss drugs shrink volume across food and drink; health-aligned and premium win, vice loses.

signature: The middle market collapses — shoppers split into premium and value, and anyone stuck selling undifferentiated mid-tier goods gets squeezed from both sides.

subthemes.title: The department store falls
subthemes.angle: The mid-tier anchor of retail hollows out as shoppers go luxury or discount.

subthemes.title: The value floor
subthemes.angle: Trading down powers dollar, convenience, and value formats.

subthemes.title: The premium ceiling
subthemes.angle: Affluent shoppers keep spending on jewelry, beauty, and status goods.

subthemes.title: Apparel splits
subthemes.angle: Fast-fashion and luxury grow; mid-price apparel chains close.

subthemes.title: Footwear & the niche
subthemes.angle: Specialty and athletic footwear thrive; generic mid-tier shoe retail shrinks.

subthemes.title: Dining bifurcates
subthemes.angle: Casual-dining middle empties as diners split between cheap fast food and premium experiences.

subthemes.title: Hotels pick a lane
subthemes.angle: Budget and luxury/experiential lodging grow; the mid-scale motel struggles.

subthemes.title: Paying for the experience
subthemes.angle: Consumers trade goods for experiences and premium live events.

subthemes.title: Value's revenge: the dupe
subthemes.angle: Cheap 'dupes' and private label eat the mainstream middle of consumer goods.

subthemes.title: The hollow middle
subthemes.angle: Capstone: the middle market is hollowing out; luxury and value win, undifferentiated mid-tier loses.

signature: The store stopped being where you buy — e-commerce, marketplaces, and direct-to-consumer hollow out physical retail, and only omnichannel or the experiential niche survives.

groups.label: A · The categories that went online first

subthemes.title: Electronics go online
subthemes.angle: Commodity electronics were the first to move online; specialty stores nearly vanished.

subthemes.title: Media & hobby retail
subthemes.angle: Amazon and marketplaces gutted these categories; survivors go experiential and expert.

subthemes.title: Apparel & the try-before-you-buy problem
subthemes.angle: Clothing and shoes shift online despite fit friction; stores become showrooms.

subthemes.title: The marketplace eats the middle
subthemes.angle: The platform takes a cut of everything and sets the terms of survival for sellers.

subthemes.title: Direct-to-consumer brands
subthemes.angle: Brands sell straight to shoppers, cutting the retailer out entirely.

subthemes.title: Omnichannel or die
subthemes.angle: Big-box survivors fuse online and store — ship-from-store, buy-online-pickup — or lose.

subthemes.title: The experiential survivor
subthemes.angle: Expertise, immediacy, and experience are the moats physical retail has left.

subthemes.title: Tariffs & the de-minimis end
subthemes.angle: Shein/Temu and the end of the de-minimis loophole reshape the price war online.

subthemes.title: The closure wave
subthemes.angle: Thousands of stores close a year; the real-estate and jobs fallout compounds.

subthemes.title: The channel shift
subthemes.angle: Capstone: the point of sale moved online; platforms and omnichannel scale win, standalone mid-market stores lose.

signature: AI's hunger for power is reshaping the grid and everything plugged into it — whoever has electricity, land, and cooling near the data centers wins a once-in-a-generation buildout.

subthemes.title: The data-center land rush
subthemes.angle: AI compute demand turns land, power, and cooling into the scarce inputs of the decade.

subthemes.title: The pipes to the internet
subthemes.angle: Connectivity and hosting ride the same demand surge underneath the AI boom.

subthemes.title: The software that runs on top
subthemes.angle: Enterprise and data software monetize the compute build-out.

subthemes.title: The generation scramble
subthemes.angle: Data centers need firm power now; gas, solar, wind, and hydro all get pulled in.

subthemes.title: The grid bottleneck
subthemes.angle: Transmission and gas delivery — not generation — become the real constraint.

groups.label: C · The physical trades of the buildout

subthemes.title: The electrical trades cash in
subthemes.angle: Electricians, cooling contractors, and turbine makers are the picks-and-shovels of compute.

subthemes.title: Concrete, steel & the shell
subthemes.angle: Data centers are also a construction-materials story — concrete, steel, and heavy build.

subthemes.title: When power gets scarce
subthemes.angle: Whoever can't get power — homes, factories, small ISPs — pays more or waits.

subthemes.title: Heat, water & the environment
subthemes.angle: Cooling water and waste heat turn into constraints and opportunities.

subthemes.title: The compute super-cycle
subthemes.angle: Capstone: AI made electricity and land scarce again; the power-and-buildout chain is the trade of the decade.

signature: Banking leaves the banks — it's embedded in apps, cards, and platforms — and scale, data, and the rails win while regional players and middlemen get squeezed.

subthemes.title: The scale game in banking
subthemes.angle: Deposits, tech, and compliance costs push banking toward a few giants.

subthemes.title: The rails that tax every swipe
subthemes.angle: Payment rails and card issuers take a cut of the whole economy's spending.

subthemes.title: The Wall Street machine
subthemes.angle: Capital markets and custody scale and financialize behind the scenes.

subthemes.title: Lending without a bank
subthemes.angle: Non-bank and embedded lenders route credit around the traditional bank.

subthemes.title: Who grades your credit
subthemes.angle: Scoring and rating is its own toll-taking layer, now AI-driven.

subthemes.title: Advice gets commoditized
subthemes.angle: Passive funds and robo-advice compress fees; scale and trust win.

subthemes.title: Moving and holding the money
subthemes.angle: Brokerage, custody, and the float are quiet, scaled, rate-sensitive businesses.

subthemes.title: The regional-bank squeeze
subthemes.angle: Rate whiplash, a CRE loan wall, and tech costs pressure smaller banks toward mergers.

subthemes.title: Living and dying by the rate
subthemes.angle: Fed rate moves reprice the whole lending stack — the swing factor for margins.

subthemes.title: Money gets unbundled
subthemes.angle: Capstone: finance splinters out of banks into rails, apps, and platforms; scale and data win, middlemen lose.

signature: Trade war and tariffs force reshoring, nearshoring, and inventory hoarding — physical supply chains get expensive and political, and whoever moves fastest to nearshore wins.

subthemes.title: The auto tariff shock
subthemes.angle: 2025 tariffs and the EV transition force the whole auto supply chain to reorder toward Mexico.

subthemes.title: The EV transition & legacy parts
subthemes.angle: Electrification voids some parts and creates others; suppliers must pick a side.

subthemes.title: Metals behind the tariff wall
subthemes.angle: Steel and aluminum tariffs ripple into every downstream builder and maker.

subthemes.title: The materials of everything
subthemes.angle: Basic materials get repriced by tariffs, energy, and reshoring.

subthemes.title: Reshoring advanced manufacturing
subthemes.angle: Defense, reshoring mandates, and supply-chain security pull advanced manufacturing home.

subthemes.title: Appliances & durable goods
subthemes.angle: Durable-goods makers weigh tariff costs against nearshoring and automation.

subthemes.title: Food's tariff exposure
subthemes.angle: Food processing and ag ride commodity and trade-war volatility.

subthemes.title: The retail import shock
subthemes.angle: Import-heavy retail eats tariff costs or passes them to shoppers.

subthemes.title: Atoms strike back
subthemes.angle: Capstone: the physical supply chain got political; nearshoring and domestic makers win, thin-margin importers lose.

signature: Capital rolls up fragmented Main Street — PE, franchises, REITs, and scale leaders absorb the independents, and financialization wins while owner-operators exit.

subthemes.title: Private equity in medicine
subthemes.angle: PE rolls up practices and clinics, chasing scale and billing power.

subthemes.title: Scale in devices & generics
subthemes.angle: Med-tech and generics consolidate to survive pricing pressure.

subthemes.title: The franchise roll-up
subthemes.angle: Franchising and PE turn local services into scaled, financialized platforms.

subthemes.title: Consolidating boring services
subthemes.angle: Professional and boring-but-essential services get rolled into regional platforms.

subthemes.title: Scale wins in retail
subthemes.angle: A few big-box leaders capture the category; independents fold.

subthemes.title: Scale in food & drink
subthemes.angle: Distribution and production consolidate; craft and independents get bought or squeezed.

subthemes.title: REITs own the ground
subthemes.angle: Institutional capital owns the real assets and rents them back.

subthemes.title: IP & catalogs as assets
subthemes.angle: Rights and catalogs get financialized into yield-bearing assets.

subthemes.title: The great consolidation
subthemes.angle: Capstone: capital rolls up the fragmented economy; scale and financialization win, independent owners exit.

signature: Hybrid work broke the office and higher rates broke the math — capital rotates from offices to logistics, data centers, and housing, and a debt wall forces the reckoning.

subthemes.title: The office crisis
subthemes.angle: Hybrid work and vacancies gut office values; a maturity wall forces losses.

subthemes.title: Adaptive reuse & conversion
subthemes.angle: Dead offices and malls get converted — a remodeling and construction opportunity.

subthemes.title: The housing squeeze
subthemes.angle: High rates freeze buying and pressure multifamily even as housing stays scarce.

subthemes.title: Logistics & data centers
subthemes.angle: Capital flows to warehouses and data centers — the assets with demand.

subthemes.title: Owning the land
subthemes.angle: Land and ground-lease models become the quiet, durable real-estate bet.

subthemes.title: Hotels as real estate
subthemes.angle: Lodging bifurcates and gets financialized as an asset class.

subthemes.title: Retail's property fallout
subthemes.angle: Store closures dump retail real estate onto the market for reuse.

subthemes.title: The commercial-debt wall
subthemes.angle: A wave of maturing CRE loans refinancing at higher rates is the sector's tail risk.

subthemes.title: Building costs bite
subthemes.angle: Tariffs, labor, and rates raise the cost to build anything new.

subthemes.title: The real-estate reckoning
subthemes.angle: Capstone: work and rates broke the old real-estate math; logistics, data, and housing win, offices lose.

signature: A patchwork of AI, privacy, climate, and cyber rules turns compliance into a rising cost — it favors scale, feeds the consultants, and prices out the small operator.

subthemes.title: The bank compliance load
subthemes.angle: Capital, KYC, and consumer rules make compliance a moat for big banks.

subthemes.title: Insurance & the regulators
subthemes.angle: State-by-state rules and new risks make insurance a compliance-heavy, data-heavy game.

subthemes.title: Healthcare's paperwork machine
subthemes.angle: Regulation and reimbursement rules make admin a huge, growing cost center.

subthemes.title: Data, privacy & cyber
subthemes.angle: Privacy and cyber rules raise the cost of holding data — and create a security market.

subthemes.title: Who profits from the rules
subthemes.angle: Lawyers, auditors, and accountants sell the compliance the rules require.

subthemes.title: Environmental & climate rules
subthemes.angle: Climate and environmental mandates create work and cost in equal measure.

subthemes.title: The small-operator squeeze
subthemes.angle: Compliance cost is fixed, so it hits small firms hardest and pushes consolidation.

subthemes.title: Governing the algorithms
subthemes.angle: New AI-governance rules land first on data, credit, and software.

subthemes.title: The compliance tax
subthemes.angle: Capstone: rules multiply into a tax that favors scale and feeds advisors; small operators pay the most.

signature: Labor, materials, energy, and tariffs rise faster than pricing power — margins compress, and only the automated, the premium, or the locked-in escape the squeeze.

subthemes.title: The food-producer squeeze
subthemes.angle: Commodity, labor, and energy costs outrun what packaged-food makers can charge.

subthemes.title: The sweet-goods squeeze
subthemes.angle: Cocoa, sugar, and dairy inflation crush indulgent-category margins.

groups.label: B · Serving food at a loss-leader price

subthemes.title: The restaurant margin trap
subthemes.angle: Wage and food inflation collide with price-sensitive diners.

subthemes.title: The drinks squeeze
subthemes.angle: Input costs and flat demand compress beverage margins.

groups.label: C · Where the lock-in defends the margin

subthemes.title: The lock-in defense
subthemes.angle: Captive locations and bundles defend margin where switching is hard.

subthemes.title: Utility-like resilience
subthemes.angle: Regulated, contracted, or essential businesses hold margin better.

subthemes.title: Automating the cost away
subthemes.angle: Automation is the main lever left to protect margin from labor inflation.

subthemes.title: Premium as the shield
subthemes.angle: Trading up to premium is the other way to keep pricing power.

subthemes.title: The margin vise
subthemes.angle: Capstone: costs rise faster than prices; automate, premiumize, or lock customers in — or watch margin vanish.

signature: Medicare cuts and payer power strip pricing from providers and device makers — volume rises with aging, but the price per unit keeps falling, and only scale survives.

subthemes.title: Death by reimbursement cut
subthemes.angle: Year after year, Medicare trims the rate while costs rise — a structural margin squeeze.

subthemes.title: The specialist squeeze
subthemes.angle: Specialists face flat reimbursement and rising costs, pushing them into groups.

subthemes.title: The device price grind
subthemes.angle: Hospital consolidation and payers grind device prices down 1-2% a year.

subthemes.title: Generic-drug deflation
subthemes.angle: Relentless price erosion in generics rewards only the largest, lowest-cost makers.

groups.label: C · The payers hold the power

subthemes.title: Who holds the purse
subthemes.angle: Insurers and Medicare Advantage set prices and squeeze everyone downstream.

subthemes.title: The independent-practice exodus
subthemes.angle: Solo and small practices sell to systems and PE to survive the pricing squeeze.

subthemes.title: Volume up, price down
subthemes.angle: Aging drives volume, but falling per-unit prices and wage costs eat the gains.

subthemes.title: The value-based bet
subthemes.angle: Shifting to value-based, lower-cost sites of care is the industry's escape hatch.

subthemes.title: The pricing-power collapse
subthemes.angle: Capstone: reimbursement and payer power strip pricing from healthcare; volume grows but only scale survives.
